dm.summary: I looked first without reloading. The desk was current: every player roll from the round was in the log, along with Bram's Adrenaline Rush, Ada's Stitch, Dev's Great Wards and Train, and Cass's Edit-sheet line. The timer was running live, and Cass's card said "changed by the player". In the story, Bram's Strike jammed the windlass and Dev's ward held. Ada's mixed Focus showed that the wet name in the fare column is her own, which cost her a Brain mark. Cass's mixed Move took her into the flooded hold for a Body mark from the water. I made an open 3-dice roll for the tide and got a 6, so the water won: Cass took two more Body marks and is at Body 3 of 3, still able to act. She did not scar, because the site only scars on a fourth mark. Then I ended it: Cass cut the ferryman's empty coat from the bell, Bram hauled her out, and Ada read the first fare, Absalom Hode's own name, so the ferryman is laid to rest. I paused the timer at 3:42, cleared it, and lowered the tension from 3 to 0; every step wrote its own log line. On the Circle page I opened the reports and ticked two Illumination questions: the source of bleed was contained, and the soaked ledger was brought back. Comfort for the afflicted is not ticked. I deliberately did not press Add Illumination yet, because it is a single press allowed once per assignment and would lose the players' keys if pressed before they file. I told the table to file their reports. I logged F090 to F093: Add Illumination is live with no reports filed and has no confirm (medium); praise for how the scene-ending steps chain and log; a full 3 of 3 track gives no warning that the next mark scars, and the handbook (third mark) and FAQ (fourth mark) disagree; and the screen reader hears "About About Reset". No console errors, and no restart was needed.

dm.story_so_far: The Whistlers crossed the Gullhaven flats, searched the ferryman's cottage and were taken aboard the ghost ferry mid-channel as the tide turned. Bram jammed the windlass and Dev's salt ward stopped the counting voice at forty-one. Ada read the fare column: the next name was her own, but the first fare, forty years back in the clerk's hand, was Absalom Hode's. The tide rolled a 6 and dragged Cass under, leaving her at Body 3 of 3, but she cut the ferryman's empty coat from the bell, Bram hauled her out, and Ada read Hode's name aloud as his own fare. The ferryman was carried over, the bell rang true once, and the ferry settled on the mud: the Ferryman's Psalm is laid to rest. The circle keeps the soaked fare ledger, which still ends in Ada's name in the slanting hand.
